lesson.titleZh: 突然感到害怕／頓時感到不安

examples.en: I went hot and cold.
examples.zh: 我頓時感到非常害怕。

examples.en: She goes hot and cold whenever she remembers the accident.
examples.zh: 她每次想起那宗意外，都會突然感到不安。

meaning.en: To experience a sudden strong feeling of fear, anxiety or worry.
meaning.zh: 突然感到一陣恐懼、不安或擔心；因為一件突如其來或令人害怕的事情而感到一陣發熱發冷。

register.summaryEn: conversation; personal stories; descriptions of frightening experiences; informal writing; interviews; fiction and narrative writing.
register.summaryZh: 這個表達屬於中性至非正式用語，尤其常見於日常對話、個人經歷、故事及對恐懼反應的描述。
register.formalEn: It can sound vivid and personal. In a highly formal medical, legal or official report, expressions such as became extremely anxious or experienced sudden fear may sometimes be more suitable.
register.formalZh: 這個表達帶有生動及個人化的感覺。 在非常正式的醫療、法律或官方報告中，became extremely anxious 或 experienced sudden fear 有時較為適合。

fixedVariable.fixedEn: Keep the fixed words and word order shown in the source expression.
fixedVariable.fixedZh: 保留原檔目標表達中的固定字詞及字序。
fixedVariable.variableEn: Change only the verb form, possessive, tense or surrounding grammar permitted by the source patterns.
fixedVariable.variableZh: 只按照原檔句式改變動詞形式、所有格、時態或前後文法。

forms.form: Subject + go / goes / went + hot and cold.
Subject + may / might / can / could / would + go hot and cold.
forms.example: You might go hot and cold when you hear what happened.

forms.form: Trigger + make / makes / made + person + go hot and cold.
forms.example: The message made me go hot and cold.

forms.form: Subject + feel / see / watch + person or reflexive pronoun + go / going hot and cold.
forms.example: I felt myself go hot and cold.

forms.form: When / whenever / as soon as / the moment + clause, subject + go / went hot and cold.
forms.example: When the door opened, I went hot and cold.

forms.form: At the thought / sight / sound of + noun or -ing, subject + go / went hot and cold.
forms.example: At the sight of smoke, the driver went hot and cold.

forms.form: On + hearing / seeing / reading / finding + object, subject + went hot and cold.
forms.example: On hearing the alarm, we went hot and cold.

forms.form: Noun phrase or that-clause + make + person + go hot and cold.
forms.example: The thought of the missing child made everyone go hot and cold.

forms.example: Adam admitted that he went hot and cold when he saw the police car.

forms.form: What + make + person + go hot and cold + be...
forms.example: What made me go hot and cold was the thought that I had sent the email to everyone.

specificForms.titleEn: As an Ordinary Finite Verb Phrase
specificForms.titleZh: 作為一般限定動詞短語
specificForms.formula: Subject + go / goes / went + hot and cold.
specificForms.descriptionEn: Went hot and cold is common because the idiom often describes one sudden past reaction. However, the past tense is not the only possible form.
specificForms.descriptionZh: 由於這個表達經常描述過去某一刻的突然反應，所以 went hot and cold 十分常見，但並不是唯一可以使用的形式。

examples.en: I went hot and cold.
examples.zh: 我頓時感到非常害怕。

examples.en: She goes hot and cold whenever she remembers the accident.
examples.zh: 她每次想起那宗意外，都會突然感到不安。

examples.en: They went hot and cold when they heard the scream.
examples.zh: 他們聽到尖叫聲時，頓時感到害怕。

specificForms.formula: Subject + may / might / can / could / would + go hot and cold.
specificForms.descriptionEn: The modal verb expresses possibility, general ability or an imagined situation. It is not part of the idiom.
specificForms.descriptionZh: 情態動詞用來表達可能性、一般情況或假設，並不是慣用語的固定部分。

examples.en: You might go hot and cold when you hear what happened.
examples.zh: 你聽到事情經過時，可能會突然感到不安。

examples.en: Anyone could go hot and cold in that situation.
examples.zh: 任何人在那種情況下都可能會突然感到害怕。

examples.en: I would go hot and cold if the police called me at midnight.
examples.zh: 如果警方在半夜致電給我，我也會頓時感到不安。

specificForms.formula: Trigger + make / makes / made + person + go hot and cold.

examples.en: The message made me go hot and cold.
examples.zh: 這則訊息令我頓時感到非常不安。

examples.en: The sound of breaking glass made her go hot and cold.
examples.zh: 玻璃碎裂的聲音令她頓時感到害怕。

examples.en: Nothing makes him go hot and cold like a late-night phone call.
examples.zh: 沒有甚麼比深夜來電更容易令他感到不安。

specificForms.formula: Subject + feel / see / watch + person or reflexive pronoun + go / going hot and cold.
specificForms.descriptionEn: Go emphasises the complete change. Going presents the reaction as it develops.
specificForms.descriptionZh: 較着重完整的突然變化； going 較着重反應正在出現的過程。

examples.en: I felt myself go hot and cold.
examples.zh: 我感到自己突然一陣發熱發冷。

examples.en: I could feel myself going hot and cold.
examples.zh: 我感覺到自己正一陣發熱發冷。

examples.en: We could see him go hot and cold when the manager mentioned the missing money.
examples.zh: 經理提到失款時，我們看得出他頓時感到非常不安。

specificForms.titleEn: With a Time or Trigger Clause
specificForms.titleZh: 配合時間或觸發情況子句
specificForms.formula: When / whenever / as soon as / the moment + clause, subject + go / went hot and cold.
specificForms.descriptionEn: These opening expressions identify the trigger. They are not fixed parts of the idiom.
specificForms.descriptionZh: 這些開首表達只用來指出觸發恐懼的事情，並不是慣用語的固定部分。

examples.en: When the door opened, I went hot and cold.
examples.zh: 門打開時，我頓時感到非常害怕。

examples.en: Whenever the doctor calls unexpectedly, he goes hot and cold.
examples.zh: 每當醫生突然致電，他都會頓時感到不安。

examples.en: The moment the lights went out, the children went hot and cold.
examples.zh: 燈光熄滅的一刻，孩子們頓時感到害怕。

specificForms.formula: At the thought / sight / sound of + noun or -ing, subject + go / went hot and cold.
specificForms.descriptionEn: Rachel went hot and cold at the thought of losing her passport.
specificForms.descriptionZh: 瑞秋一想到可能遺失護照，便頓時感到不安。

examples.en: At the sight of smoke, the driver went hot and cold.
examples.zh: 司機一看到煙便頓時感到害怕。

examples.en: At the sound of footsteps outside, I went hot and cold.
examples.zh: 我聽到門外的腳步聲時，頓時感到非常不安。

specificForms.formula: On + hearing / seeing / reading / finding + object, subject + went hot and cold.
specificForms.descriptionEn: Source grammar frame: On + hearing / seeing / reading / finding + object, subject + went hot and cold.
specificForms.descriptionZh: 原檔列出的句法框架：On + hearing / seeing / reading / finding + object, subject + went hot and cold。

examples.en: On hearing the alarm, we went hot and cold.
examples.zh: 我們一聽到警報便頓時感到害怕。

examples.en: On seeing the empty bag, Daniel went hot and cold.
examples.zh: 丹尼爾一看到空袋子便頓時感到不安。

examples.en: On reading the first line, she went hot and cold.
examples.zh: 她一讀到第一行便突然感到害怕。

specificForms.titleEn: With an Event, Thought or Message as the Subject
specificForms.titleZh: 以事件、想法或訊息作主語
specificForms.formula: Noun phrase or that-clause + make + person + go hot and cold.
specificForms.descriptionEn: The grammatical subject identifies the cause of the reaction.
specificForms.descriptionZh: 句子的主語指出造成恐懼反應的原因。

examples.en: The thought of the missing child made everyone go hot and cold.
examples.zh: 想到孩子失蹤，所有人都頓時感到害怕。

examples.en: The news that her dog was missing made Sophie go hot and cold.
examples.zh: 愛犬失蹤的消息令蘇菲頓時感到非常不安。

examples.en: To think that I might have deleted the file makes me go hot and cold.
examples.zh: 一想到自己可能刪除了檔案，我便感到非常害怕。

specificForms.formula: Subject + say / admit / explain / remember + that + subject + went hot and cold.
specificForms.descriptionEn: Source grammar frame: Subject + say / admit / explain / remember + that + subject + went hot and cold.
specificForms.descriptionZh: 原檔列出的句法框架：Subject + say / admit / explain / remember + that + subject + went hot and cold。

examples.en: Adam admitted that he went hot and cold when he saw the police car.
examples.zh: 亞當承認，看到警車時他頓時感到不安。

examples.en: She said that she had gone hot and cold when the doctor called.
examples.zh: 她說醫生來電時，自己頓時感到非常不安。

examples.en: I remember that I went hot and cold when the door moved.
examples.zh: 我記得門移動時，自己頓時感到害怕。

specificForms.titleZh: 用於強調句及疑問結構
specificForms.formula: What + make + person + go hot and cold + be...
specificForms.descriptionEn: The target expression remains unchanged inside these larger structures.
specificForms.descriptionZh: 即使放進較複雜的句式，目標慣用語本身仍然不變。

examples.en: What made me go hot and cold was the thought that I had sent the email to everyone.
examples.zh: 令我頓時感到害怕的，是我可能把電郵傳送給了所有人這個想法。

examples.en: It was the scream that made everyone go hot and cold.
examples.zh: 正是那一下尖叫聲令所有人頓時感到害怕。

examples.en: What could make you go hot and cold?
examples.zh: 甚麼事情可能會令你頓時感到害怕？

benefits.titleEn: It Expresses a Sudden Reaction Clearly
benefits.en: The idiom packages a longer emotional description into one vivid expression.
benefits.zh: 我頓時感到非常害怕。 這個慣用語把較長的情緒描述濃縮成一個生動表達。

examples.en: I went hot and cold.
examples.zh: 我頓時感到非常害怕。

benefits.titleEn: It Connects an Event with an Emotional Effect
benefits.titleZh: 把事件與情緒後果連繫起來
benefits.en: the trigger: the message; the person affected: me; the reaction: sudden fear.
benefits.zh: 這則訊息令我頓時感到不安。 句子清楚指出觸發事件、受影響的人以及突然出現的恐懼反應。

examples.en: The message made me go hot and cold.
examples.zh: 這則訊息令我頓時感到不安。

benefits.titleEn: It Makes Personal Stories More Vivid
benefits.zh: 門柄開始轉動時，我頓時感到非常害怕。 這個表達比單純說 I was worried 更能帶出那一刻的突然反應。

examples.en: When the handle began to move, I went hot and cold.
examples.zh: 門柄開始轉動時，我頓時感到非常害怕。

benefits.titleEn: It Can Describe Memory as Well as Immediate Fear
benefits.titleZh: 既可描述當下恐懼，也可描述回憶
benefits.en: The original event may be over, but the memory can produce the same reaction.
benefits.zh: 我現在每次想起那宗意外，仍會突然感到不安。 事情可能已經過去，但回憶仍然可以引發同樣的反應。

examples.en: I still go hot and cold when I remember the accident.
examples.zh: 我現在每次想起那宗意外，仍會突然感到不安。

benefits.titleEn: It Supports Several Natural Grammar Patterns
benefits.zh: 這個慣用語可以自然放進多種不同句式，而不需要把所有答案寫成同一種格式。

benefits.titleEn: It Helps Students Understand Authentic British English
benefits.titleZh: 有助理解真實英式英語
benefits.en: However, it is not automatically better than afraid, anxious or worried. Use it when the fear is sudden and vivid.
benefits.zh: 不過，它並不一定比 afraid、anxious 或 worried 更好。 只有當恐懼來得突然而且反應強烈時，才適合使用。

origin.statusEn: Exact Origin Unknown; Probable Gradual Development
origin.statusZh: 確切來源不明；很可能逐漸形成

history.en: The authoritative learner dictionaries consulted explain the modern meaning but do not connect the exact expression with one confirmed historical event or one identifiable creator. It is therefore safer to treat it as a phrase that probably developed gradually from descriptions of bodily reactions to fear. This is a cautious linguistic inference rather than a proven origin story.
history.zh: 所查閱的權威學習詞典解釋了現代意思，但沒有把這個確切表達連繫到一件已證實的歷史事件或某一位可以確認的創作者。 因此，較穩妥的說法是：這個短語很可能由人們對恐懼時身體反應的描述逐漸形成。 這是一項審慎推論，而不是已證實的來源故事。

history.en: The words hot and cold originally describe opposite temperatures. In the idiom, they work together as an image of a sudden, uncomfortable change in the body caused by fear or worry.
history.zh: hot 和 cold 原本描述相反的溫度。 在這個慣用語中，兩者結合成一個意象，表示恐懼或不安令身體突然產生不舒服的變化。

origin.memoryEn: A frightening thought makes the body seem to change from hot to cold in an instant.
origin.memoryZh: 一個可怕的念頭，彷彿令身體在一瞬間由熱變冷。

rules.titleZh: 規則一：保持 hot and cold 不變
rules.en: The contrast between hot and cold forms one fixed image.
rules.zh: hot 與 cold 的對比構成一個固定意象。

rules.titleZh: 規則二：按句法改變 go

rules.titleEn: Do Not Confuse It with “Blow Hot and Cold”
rules.titleZh: 規則三：不要與 blow hot and cold 混淆
rules.en: sudden fear or worry frequently change one’s opinion or attitude The company blew hot and cold about the plan for six months.
rules.zh: 突然感到恐懼或不安反覆改變意見或態度公司在六個月內對該計劃的態度反覆不定。

rules.titleEn: Use It for a Sudden Reaction
rules.titleZh: 規則四：用於突然出現的反應
rules.en: The idiom normally presents fear as a sudden reaction rather than a mild, continuous concern.
rules.zh: 我看到空着的床時，頓時感到非常害怕。 這個慣用語通常形容突然出現的恐懼，而不是持續數月的輕微擔心。

examples.en: When I saw the empty bed, I went hot and cold.
examples.zh: 我看到空着的床時，頓時感到非常害怕。

rules.titleEn: The Trigger Must Be Frightening or Worrying
rules.titleZh: 規則五：觸發事件必須令人害怕或擔心
rules.en: a late-night phone call; a police officer saying your name; a missing child or pet; an unexpected hospital message; a strange noise; an emergency alarm; the thought that an important item is missing; suddenly realising that something has gone wrong.
rules.zh: 適合的觸發情況包括深夜來電、警員叫出自己的名字、孩子或寵物失蹤、醫院突然來電、奇怪聲音、緊急警報，或突然察覺事情出錯。

rules.titleEn: Do Not Use It for Ordinary Temperature Changes
rules.titleZh: 規則六：不要用來描述一般溫度變化
rules.en: The literal sentence describes water temperature and is not the target meaning.
rules.zh: 花灑的水一時熱、一時冷。 我聽到有人嘗試開門時，頓時感到非常害怕。 第一句描述水溫，並不是本課教授的慣用意思。

examples.en: The shower water went hot and cold.
examples.zh: 花灑的水一時熱、一時冷。

examples.en: I went hot and cold when I heard someone trying to open the door.
examples.zh: 我聽到有人嘗試開門時，頓時感到非常害怕。

rules.titleEn: Use a Human or Feeling Subject
rules.titleZh: 規則七：主語通常是能感受恐懼的人
rules.en: A group of people may be used as the subject when the members share the reaction.
rules.zh: 當一群人同時產生這種反應時，也可以把群體作為主語。

rules.titleZh: 規則八：保留時態及可能性
rules.en: The incorrect answer changes a possible future reaction into a completed past event.
rules.zh: 錯誤答案把未來可能出現的反應，改成了已經發生的過去事件。

rules.titleZh: 規則九：在 make 之後使用原形動詞
rules.zh: 在 make 之後使用原形動詞

rules.titleEn: Do Not Repeat the Same Meaning
rules.titleZh: 規則十：不要重複相同意思
rules.en: Go hot and cold already communicates the sudden fearful reaction. The second part unnecessarily explains the idiom again.
rules.zh: 已經包含突然感到恐懼的意思，不應在後面再次重複解釋。

rules.titleZh: 規則十一：造成恐懼的原因可以保留
rules.en: The idiom replaces the fearful reaction, not the event that caused it. The reason remains because it is independent information.
rules.zh: 這個慣用語取代的是恐懼反應，而不是造成恐懼的事件。 我以為錢包不見了，頓時感到非常不安。 原因屬於獨立資料，因此需要保留。

examples.en: I went hot and cold because I thought my wallet was missing.
examples.zh: 我以為錢包不見了，頓時感到非常不安。

rules.titleZh: 規則十二：自然使用，不要過度使用
rules.en: is tired; is slightly nervous; changes their mind; dislikes something; becomes angry.
rules.zh: 只有當某人因意外、危險或令人擔心的事情而突然感到強烈恐懼或不安時，才適合使用這個表達。

instructions.en: Rewrite or respond to each item using go hot and cold. Change go into the correct form where necessary.
instructions.zh: 使用 go hot and cold 改寫句子或完成回應。 請按主語、時態及語境改變 go 的形式。

questions.prompt: When the phone rang after midnight, I suddenly felt a strong wave of fear.
questions.promptZh: 電話在半夜後響起時，我頓時感到非常害怕。

questions.answerZh: 電話在半夜後響起時，我頓時感到非常害怕。
questions.targetMeaning: To experience a sudden strong feeling of fear, anxiety or worry.

questions.prompt: The message from the hospital caused Nora to feel suddenly frightened.
questions.promptZh: 醫院傳來的訊息令諾拉頓時感到害怕。
questions.answer: The message from the hospital made Nora go hot and cold.
questions.answerZh: 醫院傳來的訊息令諾拉頓時感到害怕。
questions.targetMeaning: To experience a sudden strong feeling of fear, anxiety or worry.

questions.prompt: Ben suddenly felt extremely worried when he thought that he might have lost his passport.

questions.prompt: The sudden alarm caused all of us to feel a rush of fear.
questions.promptZh: 突然響起的警報令我們所有人頓時感到害怕。

questions.targetMeaning: To experience a sudden strong feeling of fear, anxiety or worry.

questions.prompt: Olivia suddenly became anxious when the teacher asked to see her after class.

questions.answerZh: 老師要求課後見奧利維亞時，她頓時感到非常不安。
questions.targetMeaning: To experience a sudden strong feeling of fear, anxiety or worry.

questions.prompt: Whenever I hear footsteps outside my door at night, I suddenly become frightened.
questions.promptZh: 每當我在晚上聽到門外有腳步聲，都會頓時感到害怕。

questions.answerZh: 每當我在晚上聽到門外有腳步聲，都會頓時感到害怕。
questions.targetMeaning: To experience a sudden strong feeling of fear, anxiety or worry.

questions.promptZh: 司機看到汽車冒煙時，頓時感到害怕。

questions.answerZh: 看到汽車冒煙，令司機頓時感到害怕。
questions.targetMeaning: To experience a sudden strong feeling of fear, anxiety or worry.

questions.prompt: You might suddenly feel very worried if the bank called about a payment you did not make.
questions.promptZh: 如果銀行致電查詢一筆並非由你支付的款項，你可能會頓時感到非常不安。
questions.answer: You might go hot and cold if the bank called about a payment you did not make.
questions.answerZh: 如果銀行致電查詢一筆並非由你支付的款項，你可能會頓時感到非常不安。
questions.targetMeaning: To experience a sudden strong feeling of fear, anxiety or worry.

questions.prompt: The thought that the child might be missing caused everyone to feel sudden fear.
questions.promptZh: 想到孩子可能失蹤，所有人都頓時感到害怕。
questions.answer: The thought of the missing child made everyone go hot and cold.
questions.answerZh: 想到孩子可能失蹤，令所有人頓時感到害怕。
questions.targetMeaning: To experience a sudden strong feeling of fear, anxiety or worry.

questions.prompt: When the lift stopped between two floors, we suddenly felt extremely anxious.
questions.promptZh: 升降機停在兩層樓之間時，我們頓時感到非常不安。
questions.answer: When the lift stopped between two floors, we went hot and cold.
questions.answerZh: 升降機停在兩層樓之間時，我們頓時感到非常不安。
questions.targetMeaning: To experience a sudden strong feeling of fear, anxiety or worry.

questions.promptZh: 警員一叫出我的名字，我便頓時感到害怕。
questions.answer: As soon as the police officer said my name, I went hot and cold.
questions.answerZh: 警員一叫出我的名字，我便頓時感到害怕。
questions.targetMeaning: To experience a sudden strong feeling of fear, anxiety or worry.

questions.prompt: A strange noise upstairs caused Leo to become suddenly frightened.
